hook.line: This is what AI looked like 3 years ago
hook.visual: Letterboxed early AI clip of a stand-up comic in a blue suit gesturing wildly, under a static white title with a shocked emoji; dissolves into a laughing AI crowd.

beats.what: AI comedian on a stage delivers a nonsense line; static title above the clip.
Morph-dissolve into a crowd of warped, screaming audience faces.
Comedian returns with a meaningless joke about socks in the washing machine.
Crowd shot degrades into a mass of melting raised arms.
Extreme close-up of a grinning mouth with too many teeth.
Mouth close-up deforms further, gums and teeth stretching.
The image collapses into an abstract wall of teeth-like shapes.
Ends on near-abstract grey forms, which loops back to the comedian.

characters.enters: Already on stage in the first frame, mid-gesture.
characters.acts: Delivers fake jokes in a synthetic voice while his face and the audience morph and glitch.
characters.exits: Dissolves into crowd shots and then into teeth and abstract shapes.

why_it_works: The uncanny visuals are the joke: each morph gets weirder, so the viewer keeps watching to see how bad it gets.
One-line title sets the frame (then vs now) with zero effort to read, and the caption fills in the history for people who want it.
High loop score (0.94): the abstract ending flows back into the opening comic, so many views are replays.
weaknesses: Repost of someone else's footage with no original commentary or face, so it builds no creator brand.
Speech is sparse (silence 68%) and audio is nonsense, so there is no information to save or share beyond the shock.
No comparison to today's output is shown, even though the caption promises the contrast.
for_robert: Use a then-vs-now reveal: a short clip of glitchy old AI output as a cutaway Fred reacts to in horror, then cut back to Robert. Avoid building a whole reel from reposted footage.
